text: Tenure is the length of time someone holds an office or job. Mr Abbott's long tenure as governor gave Democrats many years of his decisions to attack.
Abysmal means extremely bad, as if without a bottom, from the word abyss. The Economist calls Ken Paxton an abysmal candidate, meaning a very weak one.
Tempered means softened or held in check by something else, a word borrowed from toughening steel with heat. Democrats' thrill is tempered by the knowledge that this year was unusual.
A popular saying that Texas, a huge state, does everything on a grand scale. Ms Hinojosa uses it to joke about how big the surprise of her win was.
A speech a winning candidate gives on election night to thank supporters. Ms Hinojosa gave hers after beating the long-serving governor.
The office of governor, the top elected official of a US state. Democrats won it in Texas for the first time in decades.
A gathering where supporters follow election results together on screens. Staffers at Mr Talarico's refreshed results pages in disbelief.
A glitch is a small technical fault. The staffers thought the strong early-voting numbers must be a glitch because they seemed too good to be true.
Pundits are commentators who give opinions on politics in the news. They had expected Mr Talarico to win only narrowly.
Bleary-eyed means with tired, unfocused eyes, usually from lack of sleep. These Texans stayed up past midnight celebrating.
To sweep an election means to win nearly every contest. Here Democrats won most offices on the ballot, not just one or two.
Elected leaders chosen by voters across a whole state, such as the governor, attorney-general and comptroller, rather than by one district.
In politics, to flip a seat or county means to take it from the other party. Democrats flipped the Texas House and three suburban counties.
To outspend someone is to spend more money than they do. Republicans spent over twice as much as Democrats and still lost.
An upset is an unexpected win by the side expected to lose. Calling this a stunning upset means few predicted it.
A red state is one that reliably votes Republican, since red is the Republican color on maps. Its counterpart, a blue state, leans Democratic.
The margin is the gap between the winner's votes and the loser's. A margin over 20 points means a landslide.
The government's efforts to find, detain and deport people in the country illegally. Some voters were dismayed by the tactics used.
Dismay is a feeling of distress or disappointment. Voters' dismay with the economy and enforcement tactics sent them back to Democrats.
Suburbs are residential areas just outside a big city. Collin, Denton and Tarrant counties are suburbs north of Dallas that long leaned Republican.
To gerrymander is to redraw district borders so your party wins more seats. Texas Republicans did it last year, yet Democrats won four of those five seats anyway.
Ostensibly means apparently or supposedly, hinting the real reason may differ. The new map was supposed to help Republicans, but it didn't.
The chairman runs a party's organization, raising money and helping candidates, though he is not a government official. Kendall Scudder leads the Texas one.
A stock insult for politicians who supposedly raise taxes to fund big government. Mr Scudder says Texas Democrats are not like that.
To perpetuate something is to keep it going. Mr Scudder says Fox News keeps spreading myths about Democrats.
A steward looks after something that belongs to others. Responsible stewards of public money means spending it carefully.
To dispel is to make something, like a false belief, disappear. Mr Scudder wants to dispel myths about Democrats.
Texas law strictly limits abortion. Democrats were asked whether they'd roll it back, and the chairman did not directly answer.
A major law passed under President Trump that included spending cuts, notably to health care. Democrats hope to reverse the cuts.
Uninsured people have no health insurance and may struggle to pay for care. Texas has the highest rate in the country.
The Republican governor of Texas for three terms, defeated by Ms Hinojosa.
Constraints are limits on what someone can do. A Texas governor's power is limited by the legislature and by officials she can't fire.
Resembling the style of Donald Trump, such as bold, headline-grabbing promises. Here it describes a promise to send cash to every household.
Ms Hinojosa's name for her plan to send households $1,500, suggesting it returns money lost to corruption. It could cost $17bn.
To sack someone means to fire them. The governor can't sack the roughly 2,500 officials who run state agencies.
Texas's top civil court has nine justices. Seven were appointed by Mr Abbott, so the courts lean toward his views.
To dismantle means to take something apart piece by piece. Ms Hinojosa plans to undo many of Mr Abbott's policies.
Huge buildings full of computers that store and process online information. They use lots of electricity and water, so some voters resist them.
A critics' term for government help to businesses, like tax breaks. Businesses fear Ms Hinojosa will end them.
Reductions in taxes offered to encourage something, such as a company building in a state.
A voucher is public money families can spend on private school tuition. Texas launched a $1bn program this autumn, which Democrats fought bitterly.
The state's chief financial officer, who tracks and reports on money coming in and going out. Sarah Eckhardt will examine funding for private schools.
To scrutinise is to examine very closely, looking for problems.
Laws designed to stop officials from misusing power or taking bribes.
Taxes paid by owners of homes and land, mostly funding schools and local services. They rose 86% under Mr Abbott.
The state's top lawyer, who can sue on its behalf. Nathan Johnson may join other states suing the Trump administration.
States that lean Democratic. The Economist calls it surreal to include Texas.
Surreal describes something so strange it feels like a dream.
A lobbyist is paid to persuade lawmakers on behalf of a group or company. Jason Sabo is a Democratic one in Austin.
A figurative way of saying suffering repeated defeats. Mr Sabo means Democrats lost for 30 years.
Hiring more workers. The new officials must quickly build teams to run their offices.
Here muscle means strength in people and organization needed to get things done.
The ceremony where an elected leader formally takes office. Mr Scudder joked he must plan one.
Held in check by something else, as joy can be cooled by worry.
Angst is a feeling of anxiety or frustration, often about the future. Voters' angst made them want change.
Rich people who give large sums to campaigns.
A comeback is a return to strength after a defeat.
A lasting shift in which groups of voters support which party. One year's wave doesn't prove it.
A nickname for Texas, from the single star on its flag.
A political scientist at Southern Methodist University in Dallas whom the Economist quotes about Texas politics.
